newsitem.title: USA: SEC to hold meeting on move to decimal quotes.
newsitem.headline: SEC to hold meeting on move to decimal quotes.

text.p: Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Arthur Levitt said Thursday the agency will hold a meeting of industry officials within the next 30 days to coordinate the shift in trading to decimal quotes.
"There are many important technical issues that still need to be addressed," Levitt said in a statement.
Most stocks are traded in eigths or sixteenths of a dollar, so the smallest trading increment is either 12.5 cents or 6.25 cents, respectively.
Switching to decimals, could, in theory, allow these spreads to shrink to as little as one cent.

"This should be an industry-wide coordinated effort and for that reason I am calling a meeting with all of the markets, clearance organizations, and industry officials with the next 30 days to begin this process," Levitt said.
Levitt also said there are timing issues that must be considered to ensure a smooth and orderly transition.
